sb_prompt: WHAT DO YOU THINK ABOUT CURRENT OR RECENT AMERICAN ACTIONS IN LATIN AMERICA
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantB: Sorry, wrong number?
ParticipantA: Nah, my friend told me to call a stranger about Latin America.
ParticipantB: Oh, cool. Okay.
ParticipantA: So, what do you think about current or recent American actions in Latin America?
ParticipantB: Hmm. Honestly? I don't really follow the news that much unless it's a leak.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I get that. But sometimes it feels like the U.S. is trying to police the whole continent without asking.
ParticipantB: Exactly. It feels invasive. Like we're just stepping in everywhere.
ParticipantA: Tell me more. Why does it feel that way to you?
ParticipantB: Well, I'm a plumber, and I've been working here for years.
ParticipantA: Oh? That's interesting.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I made up my mind about plumbing years ago, just felt like it was what I was supposed to do.
ParticipantA: That makes sense. People just gravitate toward trades sometimes.
ParticipantB: Anyway, when I work, I see things from the ground up. And lately, I've noticed more American contractors showing up where they shouldn't be.
ParticipantA: Wait, really? Like in Mexico or Colombia?
ParticipantB: Yeah. Like, they're buying up old infrastructure and renaming it, or sending in "advisors" who just tell people how to fix their pipes.
ParticipantA: Wow. That sounds really heavy. I actually work as a restaurant server, so I hear these stories all the time from my regulars.
ParticipantB: Oh? What kind of stories?
ParticipantA: Well, one of my regulars used to be a volunteer in Guatemala. He came back and said the Americans were pushing a drug crackdown so hard it's destabilizing whole towns.
ParticipantB: That's scary. I've had clients tell me their governments feel pressured to do things that hurt their own economy just to please Washington.
ParticipantA: It does seem like we're losing our sovereignty a bit. It feels like the U.S. thinks they know better than local people what's good for their own countries.
ParticipantB: Totally. It's like if I walked into your house and started telling you how to fix your sink because I have a wrench.
ParticipantA: Haha, fair point! But seriously, do you think that will change anytime soon?
ParticipantB: Doubtful. I feel like the momentum is just too strong. We made our bed years ago, and now we're stuck in it.
ParticipantA: Yeah, me too. I don't know if we'll ever get out of this dynamic.
ParticipantB: Maybe not. But at least we're talking about it out loud instead of just accepting it.
ParticipantA: True. Thanks for chatting, stranger.
ParticipantB: No problem. Good luck with your shift.
ParticipantA: You too. Bye!
